A Lie algebra over a field is a vector space g with a bilinear operation [x,y], called the Lie bracket, that is alternating and satisfies the Jacobi identity.

Cartan's criterion

Words: 35
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, Cartan's criterion characterizes a solvable Lie algebra by vanishing of its Killing form on g×[g,g], and a semisimple Lie algebra by nondegeneracy of that form. The Cartan solvability criterion and Cartan criterion for semisimplicity state the two distinct tests.

Loop algebra (Lg=g⊗k​k[t,t−1])

Words: 72
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The algebraic loop algebra of a Lie algebra g over a field k consists of finite Laurent polynomials with coefficients in g. Its Lie bracket is [x⊗tm,y⊗tn]=[x,y]⊗tm+n, extended bilinearly. Alternation and the Jacobi identity follow from those of g, since the Laurent polynomial ring is commutative. Appropriate smooth or formal completions give other loop-algebra variants; the affine current algebra adds a central extension to these Fourier modes. For the affine extension, see Kac and Wakimoto, Section 0.2.

Affine current algebra ([Jma​,Jnb​]=ifabcJm+nc​+kmδm+n,0​δab)

Words: 67
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The affine current algebra is the one-dimensional central extension of the loop algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra, with central element acting as the level k. A restricted module has Jn​v=0 for all sufficiently large n for each vector v; this makes the Sugawara construction finite on each vector after normal ordering. In a compact unitary positive-energy representation, the nontrivial integrable levels are positive integers in the standard basic normalization.

Free Lie algebra (LR​(X))

Words: 97 Articles: 1
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The Lie algebra over a commutative ring R generated by a set X subject only to bilinearity, alternation and the Jacobi identity. Every map from X to the underlying set of an R-Lie algebra extends uniquely to a Lie algebra homomorphism. It can be constructed from bracketed words by quotienting by those identities; elements are represented by Lie polynomials.

Lie polynomial

Words: 44
Free Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
A finite linear combination of iterated Lie brackets in formal variables. It evaluates naturally in every Lie algebra, and every Lie algebra homomorphism preserves its evaluation. The homogeneous terms of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff formula are rational Lie polynomials; this permits the group law to be reconstructed from the bracket wherever the series converges.

Semidirect product of Lie algebras (a⋊b)

Words: 61
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
If D:b→Der(a) is a Lie algebra homomorphism into the derivations of a Lie algebra, the semidirect product has underlying vector space a⊕b and bracket [(a,b),(a′,b′)]=([a,a′]+Db​a′−Db′​a,[b,b′]). The homomorphism and derivation identities ensure the Jacobi identity. The first factor is an ideal; the second is a subalgebra whose action records the twisting. The diamond Lie algebra arises by letting a one-dimensional algebra act on a Heisenberg Lie algebra.

Lie algebra cohomology (Hk(g,V))

Words: 107 Articles: 1
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The Chevalley-Eilenberg complex consists of alternating maps from gk to a Lie algebra representation V, with differential built from the bracket and module action. For trivial real coefficients, a two-cocycle is an alternating bilinear form κ satisfying κ([X,Y],Z)+κ([Y,Z],X)+κ([Z,X],Y)=0. Engel's theorem OurBigBook.com
First prove the Engel lemma by induction on the dimension of a Lie algebra of nilpotent endomorphisms. If xm=0, then adx=Lx​−Rx​ on the endomorphism algebra has (adx)2m−1=0, since left and right multiplication commute. Thus a proper Lie subalgebra M acts nilpotently on L/M, and induction gives a nonzero class normalized by M. This proves the Engel normalizer lemma.
For a maximal proper M, its normalizer is all of L, so M is an ideal. Maximality then forces dimL/M=1, since every line in a Lie algebra is a subalgebra. Induction gives a nonzero common annihilator W of M in the representation space. Ideality makes W stable under L. A generator x of L/M is nilpotent on W and has nonzero kernel there, providing a vector killed by all of L. In the possibly nonfaithful quotient actions, apply induction to the image, whose dimension is at most dimM.
Repeatedly apply this common-kernel statement to quotient representation spaces to obtain a complete flag with xVj​⊆Vj−1​. Hence the operators are simultaneously strictly upper triangular. Applying this to the Adjoint representation shows that a finite-dimensional Lie algebra whose every adjoint map is nilpotent has terminating lower central series. Conversely, termination of that series immediately makes every adjoint map nilpotent. This proves Engel theorem.

Since ca​mn is antisymmetric in m,n, only the commutator part of the cubic trace tensor of a Lie algebra representation contributes, proving ca​mnBmnb​=−Hab​/2. In an adapted compact basis with κab​=−δab​ and Hab​=−μδab​, the resulting sign is positive: +μδab​/2. Defining the lowered structure constants with a positive Euclidean metric instead would reverse this sign.
// Target: lie-theory.bigb
Invariance identity for a cubic trace tensor
Words: 20
Cubic trace tensor of a Lie algebra representation OurBigBook.com
The trace of a commutator gives
B([W,X],Y,Z)+B(X,[W,Y],Z)+B(X,Y,[W,Z])=0.
(19)
In a basis, cyclicity converts this to cda​ℓBbcℓ​+cdb​ℓBcaℓ​+cdc​ℓBabℓ​=0.
// Target: lie-theory.bigb
Positive trace index for a compact simple Lie algebra (Tr(d(X)d(Y))=μκ(X,Y),μ>0)
Words: 69
Trace form of a Lie algebra representation OurBigBook.com
For a nontrivial finite-dimensional anti-Hermitian Lie algebra representation of a compact Lie algebra that is simple, its Trace form of a Lie algebra representation is a positive multiple of the Killing form. Define T by H(X,Y)=κ(TX,Y). Invariance makes T commute with the Adjoint representation of a Lie algebra. Symmetry makes T self-adjoint for −κ, so its eigenspaces are ideals. Simplicity implies T=μI. The kernel of the representation is an ideal and hence vanishes; therefore H(X,X)=−Tr(d(X)†d(X))<0 for nonzero X, proving μ>0.
// Target: lie-theory.bigb

Trace trilinear form of a Lie algebra representation (B(X,Y,Z))

Words: 33
Lie algebra representation OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional representation d, the trilinear form B(X,Y,Z)=Tr(d(X)d(Y)d(Z)) is invariant under simultaneous adjoint action. This follows by writing the sum of its three infinitesimal variations as the trace of a commutator.

Heisenberg Lie algebra

Words: 531 Articles: 13
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The three-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra has a basis a,b,c with [a,b]=c and c central. It is a two-step nilpotent Lie algebra.

Heisenberg group

Words: 480 Articles: 11
Heisenberg Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The real Heisenberg group consists of upper-unitriangular 3×3 real matrices. In coordinates (q,r,s) its multiplication is (q,r,s)(q′,r′,s′)=(q+q′,r+r′,s+s′+qr′).

Center quotient of the real Heisenberg group (H/Z(H)≅(R2,+))

Words: 38
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
In coordinates h(x,y,z)=(100​x10​yz1​), the Heisenberg group law is h(x,y,z)h(a,b,c)=h(x+a,y+b+xc,z+c). Commutation for every (a,b,c) forces xc=az, hence x=z=0. The center of a group is therefore the y-axis. The surjective group homomorphism h(x,y,z)↦(x,z) has exactly this kernel of a group homomorphism, giving the stated quotient group by the first isomorphism theorem.

Right-invariant coframe of the real Heisenberg group (dx,dy,dz−ydx)

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
For the Heisenberg group law (x,y,z)(a,b,c)=(x+a,y+b,z+c+xb), the right Maurer-Cartan form has coefficients dx,dy,dz−ydx. They satisfy dσ1=dσ2=0 and dσ3=σ1∧σ2. A general right-invariant Riemannian metric is a constant positive-definite symmetric matrix in this coframe.
Killing frame for a right-invariant Heisenberg metric (∂x​,∂y​+x∂z​,∂z​)
Words: 37
Right-invariant coframe of the real Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
Every right-invariant Riemannian metric on the Heisenberg group has Killing vector fields ∂x​, ∂y​+x∂z​ and ∂z​. Their Lie brackets of vector fields reproduce [X,Y]=Z and the central relations. Their flows are right translations. The dual frame of the right-invariant coframe is different and has the opposite Lie-bracket sign.

Modular Heisenberg group (Hp​=UT3​(Fp​))

Words: 76
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
The modular Heisenberg group consists of upper-unitriangular 3×3 matrices over the finite field Fp​. In coordinates M(x,y,z), multiplication is M(x,y,z)M(x′,y′,z′)=M(x+x′,y+y′+xz′,z+z′), and its order is p3. Its center of a group is {M(0,y,0)}≅Cp​; the quotient group by the centre is Cp​×Cp​, represented by the x,z coordinates. The elementary generators a=M(1,0,0), b=M(0,0,1), c=M(0,1,0) satisfy ap=bp=cp=e, aba−1b−1=c, and c central. For p=2, (ab)2=c, so the whole group does not have exponent two.

Left-invariant frame of the real Heisenberg group

Words: 119 Articles: 2
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
For multiplication (x,y,z)(a,b,c)=(x+a,y+b,z+c+xb), the left-invariant frame is
E1​=∂x​,E2​=∂y​+x∂z​,E3​=∂z​.
(20)
Its Lie brackets of vector fields satisfy [E1​,E2​]=E3​ and the other basis brackets vanish.
Heisenberg horizontal distribution (D=span(E1​,E2​))
Words: 99 Articles: 1
Left-invariant frame of the real Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
The horizontal smooth distribution on the real Heisenberg group is spanned by E1​=∂x​ and E2​=∂y​+x∂z​. It is not an involutive distribution because their bracket is ∂z​, but their brackets span the full tangent space. A horizontal curve satisfies x˙=α, y˙​=β, and z˙=xβ.
Smooth horizontal reachability in the real Heisenberg group
Words: 56
Heisenberg horizontal distribution OurBigBook.com
Every point (Px​,Py​,Pz​) can be reached from the identity by a smooth curve tangent to the Heisenberg horizontal distribution. Put a=2(Pz​−Px​Py​/2+Px​) and choose
α(t)=Px​+acos(2πt),β(t)=Py​+2πsin(2πt).
(21)
Their integrals give x(1)=Px​, y(1)=Py​, and z(1)=∫01​x(t)β(t)dt=Px​Py​/2−Px​+a/2=Pz​. The third coordinate measures the effect of the noncommuting horizontal directions; integrability would instead confine horizontal curves to a two-dimensional leaf.

Integer Heisenberg group (H(Z))

Words: 139 Articles: 2
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
The integer Heisenberg group consists of upper-unitriangular three-by-three integer matrices. In coordinates (x,y,z) its multiplication is
(x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′)=(x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+xy′).
(22)
It is the semidirect product Z2⋊A​Z for
A=(11​01​),
(23)
and its abelianization is Z2.
Scaled Heisenberg lattice (Nk​={(x,y,z):x,y,z∈kZ})
Words: 55
Integer Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
In the real Heisenberg group with multiplication (x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′)=(x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+xy′), the displayed set is a discrete cocompact subgroup. Writing a=(k,0,0), b=(0,k,0), c=(0,0,k) gives [a,b]=ck and c central. Hence its abelianization is Z2⊕Z/k. The right quotient maps to R2/kZ2 by its first two coordinates; each fibre is the central circle R/kZ.
Commutator identity in the integer Heisenberg group ([ar,bs]=crs)
Words: 51
Integer Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
Write the Integer Heisenberg group with central generator c=[a,b], so ab=cba. Moving a successively past powers of b gives
arbsa−rb−s=crs(r,s∈Z).
(24)
For positive exponents this follows by two inductions; inverses give the remaining signs. The representation a=I+E12​, b=I+E23​, c=I+E13​ checks the identity and shows c has infinite order.

Schrödinger representation of the Heisenberg group

Words: 25
Heisenberg group OurBigBook.com
On L2(R), translations and multiplication by phases give the Schrödinger representation of the Heisenberg group. The central coordinate acts by an overall phase.

Polynomial representation of the Heisenberg Lie algebra

Words: 32
Heisenberg Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
On C[x], the operators d/dx, multiplication by x, and the identity satisfy [d/dx,x]=1. Sending a,b,c to these operators gives a faithful irreducible infinite-dimensional representation of the Heisenberg Lie algebra.

Complexification of a Lie algebra

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
For a real Lie algebra g, its complexification is gC​=g⊗R​C with the bracket extended complex-bilinearly.

Complexification preserves semisimplicity (rad(gC​)=(radg)C​)

Words: 67
Complexification of a Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g, the solvable radical of its complexification of a Lie algebra is invariant under complex conjugation. Its real fixed subspace is a solvable ideal of g, and complexifying that fixed subspace recovers the whole radical. Conversely the complexification of any real solvable ideal is solvable. These inclusions prove the displayed identity; in particular g is semisimple if and only if gC​ is semisimple.

Universal enveloping algebra (U(g))

Words: 155 Articles: 2
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com
The universal enveloping algebra U(g) is the associative algebra generated by g subject to xy−yx=[x,y]. Its modules are the same as Lie algebra representations.

Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt theorem

Words: 130 Articles: 1
Universal enveloping algebra OurBigBook.com
For an ordered basis (xi​) of a Lie algebra g, the ordered monomials x1a1​​⋯xnan​​ form a basis of U(g). In particular, a triangular decomposition g=n−⊕t⊕n+ gives U(g)≅U(n−)⊗U(t)⊗U(n+) as vector spaces.

Semisimple Lie algebra

Words: 12k Articles: 296
Lie algebra OurBigBook.com

Graded Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem (grU(L)≅Sym(L))

Words: 86
Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt theorem OurBigBook.com
For a graded Lie algebra over characteristic zero, the associated graded algebra of its universal enveloping algebra under the word-length filtration is its graded symmetric algebra. Ordered homogeneous monomials form a basis, with exponent at most one on each odd Lie basis element. The defining graded commutation relations reorder every word, and the Jacobi identity resolves the triple-reordering ambiguities. In particular the primitive elements of a Hopf algebra of U(L) are precisely L: in its associated graded algebra, a primitive polynomial of symmetric length greater than one would have a nonzero mixed term under the diagonal, which is impossible in characteristic zero.
